transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thanks for seeing me. 

Um, I guess I'm here because I'm having a really hard time staying focused on my work. I'm a high school teacher, and I'll sit down at my desk with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, fully intending to just get through it. But then... maybe ten minutes later, I'll realize I’ve just been staring at the exact same page. My mind just wanders off, and I end up thinking about three other things instead of the work. I'm just barely taking in what’s right in front of me, and it's starting to become a real problem.
Have you experienced this kind of trouble focusing since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, it's actually been going on since I was a kid. Even back in primary school, my report cards always said things like, um, "bright but careless," or that I wouldn't finish my work unless I was closely supervised. And my parents were always finding worksheets just crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack that I had completely forgotten to turn in. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticing a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes when I fall behind on grading, but I wouldn't say I feel down or sad in general. And I still enjoy my hobbies and everything, like hiking on the weekends. It's just the focusing part that's the issue.
